strings: Every hire, every answer, every payment: someone takes a cut.
In India, getting hired, getting a straight answer and getting paid each pass through a middleman who charges at every step.
Hiring. A recruiter pays to see resumes, and a job seeker hands their phone number to everyone who asks.
Answers. Someone who wants a straight answer pays by the minute.
Payments. A small seller loses a slice of every sale.
Three public figures, each with its source and year. They show how much money already moves through middlemen. They are not our market share, and not a forecast of ours.

Noha Pay sends the money straight to the seller’s own UPI ID and never holds it. Noha Money adds one wallet for cashback and refunds. Both are open source, so anyone can read the code and run it.
People Pitchers and Kosmik take their payments through it · a hosted version for other sellers is a plan
Asanoha Store, Ayurvedic medicine on prescription, is the product we started Asanoha for. It is not open: it waits on GST registration, a licence number on every product and legal sign-off.

Our price is one flat number shown before you pay, not a cut of every step: People Pitchers Pro is ₹2,499 a seat a month before GST, and a Kosmik pass is ₹51 for 7 days or ₹101 for 30 days, never renewed by itself. Job seekers use People Pitchers for free, with 5 free AI actions a day before credits; Kosmik guests get 3 free questions a day; and anyone can run Noha Pay themselves without paying us.
A Reddit post, a classroom and a living room
None of us met at a startup event. We met the way people in India actually meet: looking for a flatmate and sitting in the same class.
Nine people answered a flatmate post
A needed a flatmate in Bengaluru and posted on Reddit. Nine people replied. S got the room.

The flatmate turned out to be the person who asks what everything costs, who will do the paperwork and whether anyone has eaten. Every team needs that person. Ours came from a Reddit thread, and today he runs operations.
A classmate who asks how everyone feels
At business school, A found J: an engineer turned HR consultant, the kind of person who asks how everyone feels, even in a meeting about fonts.
Our first product together wasn’t for investors. It was a site for our own batch, built because the timetable lived in a spreadsheet that kept changing.
Late night, chai, “yaar, hear me out”
The plan came together in a living room, laptops open. A had the idea. J asked who it was for. S asked what it would cost.
We split the work the only way that works with day jobs. Everyone owns one thing, and nobody waits for permission.
In September we had one website
We all have day jobs, so Asanoha gets the nights and the weekends.

In September we built the store site. In October we wrote seven commits. Then in November we stopped talking and started shipping: Wearday on the 6th, People Pitchers on the 10th, Kosmik on the 13th, the LLP on the 14th and our own payment rail rewritten from scratch on the 22nd.
We keep receipts. Every line on the right names a commit, a date or a registration you can check, and the public ones link to the code.

“Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Don’t let the fruit be your reason to act, and don’t hold on to doing nothing.”
We cannot promise how this ends. We can choose the work, and do it well.
That is how we build. Ideas are cheap and everyone has a few. Software that actually ships is much harder to find.
Our motive is not this platform, or even this company. We think the real work is shrinking the time between an idea and its execution, and so far that is where we have been strongest.

People Pitchers: 2,000 companies × 1.5 seats × ₹29,988 a year = ₹9.0 crore. Kosmik: 50,000 × ₹101 a month × 12 = ₹6.06 crore. Store: 20,000 customers × 4 orders a year × ₹1,200 = ₹9.6 crore. Hosted Noha Pay: 5,000 sellers × ₹499 a month × 12 = ₹3.0 crore, at a planned price. These are planning estimates, not forecasts.

Flat prices, shown before anyone pays: People Pitchers seats, Kosmik passes and report packs, and store orders once the store opens. Later, a hosted Noha Pay for other sellers at a flat monthly price. Today only Kosmik passes and reports take money.

The focus is the shared layer under the apps. Sign-in, payments, the wallet, WhatsApp messages and AI caching were built once, so a new app starts with all of them. Our measure is how fast a new idea reaches paying users and how little it costs to run. Apps that don’t earn their place will be shut down, not kept alive.
UPI made small payments cheap to take, AI lets a small team build what once needed a large one, and Indian users now expect apps in their own language.

In hiring, Naukri and LinkedIn, and test makers such as HackerRank and Mettl. In guidance, Astrotalk and other per-minute apps. In payments, gateways such as Razorpay. Each is large. We start with the part they leave to a middleman or a per-minute fee.
We ship. 558 commits since 25 September, four products and a registered LLP, all alongside day jobs. One founder writes the code, one handles people and partners, and one runs operations.

We have not yet shown that people will pay at scale: ₹102 so far. The store will sell a regulated Ayurvedic medicine, only on prescription, so it opens only after legal sign-off. WhatsApp codes run through our own relay today and should move to the official WhatsApp Business API before we scale. And several apps is a lot for three people with day jobs, which is why they share everything they can.
